cards.front: What is the classification system for varus-ankle arthritis ? Takakura
cards.extra: Stage I: shows no joint-space narrowing, but early sclerosis and osteophyte formation. Stage 2: shows narrowing of the joint space medially. Stage 3: shows obliteration of the joint space with subchondral bone contact medially. Stage 4: shows obliteration of the whole joint space with complete bone contact. Note: Stage 3a shows obliteration of the joint space that is limited in the facet to medial malleolus. Stage 3b shows obliteration of the joint space that has advanced to the roof of the talar dome. Supramalleolar osteotomy has been shown to be effective for patients in stage 2 or stage 3a, but clinical results for patients with stage 3b are unsatisfactory. On the image below, a postoperative radiograph is shown that illustrates a supramalleolar opening wedge osteotomy which was made to normalize the TAS and TT angle.
